title: Lithological / Chronostratigraphic Divisions of India
classification_scheme: Classical Blanford-Medlicott four-fold division, as used in GSI geological map legends
source_note: Compiled from GSI's traditional lithological classification and standard Indian geology textbooks (e.g. Ravindra Kumar, Krishnan). This is a coarser, map-legend-style classification layered on top of the detailed Supergroup->Group->Formation->Member hierarchy from the earlier stratigraphy files - each division here groups several of those supergroups/systems together by age and lithological character. Cross-check against the latest GSI Stratigraphic Chart of India for current usage.

divisions.name: Archaean Group
divisions.age: Eoarchean to Neoarchean / earliest Paleoproterozoic (c. 4000-2500 Ma)
divisions.lithology_character: Highly deformed and metamorphosed crystalline basement - granite, gneiss, migmatite, schist, banded iron formation (BIF), greenstone
divisions.description: Oldest exposed rocks of India, forming the crystalline basement of the Peninsular Shield on which all younger sequences were unconformably deposited.

subdivisions.name: Peninsular Gneissic Complex (PGC)
subdivisions.region: Dharwar Craton and other cratonic nuclei

subdivisions.name: Bundelkhand Gneissic Complex
subdivisions.lithology: Gneiss, granite; cut by Bundelkhand quartz reef swarm

subdivisions.name: Singhbhum Craton (Older Metamorphic Group / Singhbhum Granite)
subdivisions.lithology: Gneiss, granite, banded iron formation (Iron Ore Group)

divisions.name: Purana Group
divisions.lithology_character: Flat-lying, undeformed and largely unmetamorphosed platform sedimentary sequences - sandstone, shale, limestone/dolomite - deposited in intracratonic basins on the Archaean basement
divisions.description: 'Purana' means 'ancient' in Sanskrit; these are the oldest well-preserved sedimentary basins of Peninsular India, sitting unconformably on Archaean crystalline basement.

subdivisions.name: Cuddapah System
subdivisions.lithology: Quartzite, shale, limestone, dolomite; minor volcanics

subdivisions.name: Bhima Basin
subdivisions.related_supergroup: Bhima Supergroup (conventionally ranked as Bhima Group)

subdivisions.name: Kurnool Basin
subdivisions.related_supergroup: Kurnool Supergroup (conventionally ranked as Kurnool Group)

divisions.name: Dravidian Group
divisions.age: Cambrian to Jurassic (Paleozoic to early Mesozoic, c. 540-160 Ma)
divisions.lithology_character: Two contrasting settings - marine shelf carbonates/shales in the Extra-Peninsular Himalayan belt, and fluvio-lacustrine sandstone-shale-coal sequences in Peninsular India (Lower Gondwana)
divisions.description: Named for its type development in parts of the Peninsula; represents the interval when the Himalayan region was a passive continental shelf under the Tethys Sea while Peninsular India developed rift-basin coal-bearing sequences.

subdivisions.name: Lower Gondwana (Peninsular equivalent)
subdivisions.region: Damodar Valley, Pranhita-Godavari Valley, Son Valley, Mahanadi Valley
subdivisions.related_supergroup: Gondwana Supergroup - Damuda Group, Panchet Group (see earlier stratigraphy file)

divisions.name: Aryan Group
divisions.age: Upper Carboniferous / Jurassic to Recent (c. 300 Ma - present)
divisions.lithology_character: Varied - continental Upper Gondwana clastics, Jurassic-Cretaceous marine sequences, Deccan flood basalts, Tertiary molasse (Siwalik), and unconsolidated Quaternary alluvium/laterite
divisions.description: Youngest and most lithologically diverse division, spanning the final breakup-related and post-breakup sedimentation, the massive Deccan volcanism, Himalayan orogeny-related foreland deposits, and modern surficial deposits.

subdivisions.name: Upper Gondwana
subdivisions.related_supergroup: Gondwana Supergroup - Mahadeva Group, Rajmahal Group

subdivisions.name: Cretaceous marine sequences
subdivisions.region: Cauvery Basin, Trichinopoly (Tamil Nadu), Narmada Valley

subdivisions.name: Deccan Trap
subdivisions.lithology: Tholeiitic basalt flows, with intertrappean sedimentary beds
subdivisions.region: Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka - covers ~500,000 sq km

subdivisions.name: Tertiary sequence
subdivisions.lithology: Marine to continental clastics; Siwalik molasse in the north

subdivisions.name: Quaternary sequence
subdivisions.lithology: Alluvium, laterite, blown sand, boulder conglomerate, coastal/deltaic deposits
subdivisions.region: Indo-Gangetic Plain, coastal tracts, desert areas of Rajasthan

physiographic_lithological_provinces.note: Complementary map-based grouping used by GSI alongside the age-based divisions above; useful as a separate map layer/legend grouping

provinces.name: Peninsular Shield
provinces.description: Stable craton comprising Archaean basement plus Purana basins plus Lower Gondwana (Dravidian) cover; largely unaffected by Himalayan orogeny

provinces.name: Extra-Peninsula (Himalaya)
provinces.description: Folded and faulted marine Paleozoic-Mesozoic sequences plus Tertiary Siwalik foreland deposits, formed by the India-Asia collision

provinces.name: Indo-Gangetic Plain
provinces.description: Young Quaternary alluvial fill in the foreland basin between the Peninsular Shield and the Himalaya; no exposed bedrock
